text:
sara: Heads-up — BrightHealth just opened an escalation. After the March 10 rollout the chat widget started refusing medical advice that used to be allowed in their workflow. They say it used to return guideline-aligned suggestions, now it replies with a refusal 9/10 times. Customer thread attached and they've shared a repro. :frowning:

sara: Repro notes from BrightHealth (copied):
1) Open patient chat flow -> ask 'Can I take ibuprofen with lisinopril?'
2) Wait for assistant reply (takes < 1s normally)
3) Assistant returns: 'I'm sorry, I can't help with that' (no follow-up or escalation to human)

sara: I ran a quick local curl against the public API using their prompt and got the same refusal. Traces show `model: redwood-chat-1.2-prod` in headers. Trace id: trace-0a1b2c3d.

-- curl repro --
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-chat-1.2-prod","input":"Can I take ibuprofen with lisinopril?"}' \
  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate | jq
```

sara: Response body (shortened):
```json
{"id":"r_123","model":"redwood-chat-1.2-prod","output":"I'm sorry, I can't help with that request","safety_flag":"refusal","route":"safety_fallback"}
```

diego: Thanks for the ping. Quick questions: did the customer have any model pinning? If not, they might've been routed to a new safety-tuned variant. BrightHealth onboards with default routing. I can pull rollout metadata. :eyes:

avery: Noted. We shipped a targeted safety threshold tweak in rollout `rollout/2026-03-10-safety-tune` that adjusted moderation sensitivity for clinical prompts to reduce under-refusal on a small set of edge-case toxic examples. Canary was 10% to start. Could this have over-corrected?

jordan: I'm looking at the deploy logs. Canary started at 2026-03-10 18:07:12 UTC. Rollout metadata:
- rollout id: rollout/2026-03-10-safety-tune
- component: safety-classifier-v3
- initial canary: 10% traffic, auto-increase disabled
- config change: `safety_threshold` from 0.72 -> 0.55 for clinical domain

jordan: I also see an autoscaler bump 2026-03-10 19:01:30 that temporarily routed traffic through fallback paths; not sure if relevant.

diego: That threshold change would make the classifier more likely to mark content as unsafe (lower threshold -> more sensitive). Wait, 0.72 -> 0.55 should make it *less* likely? need to double-check sign convention.

avery: Good catch — docs say lower threshold = more permissive. Hmm. The engineer who pushed the change reported flipping the sign in the config template (we had a bug in the templating). If the value got inverted in production it could make it stricter than intended.

sara: Customer says this started immediately after they upgraded the widget (which does a model selection call) but they didn't change their config. They haven't pinned to an older model. They can repro in their environment; they recorded the assistant message exactly as above.

jordan: I pulled the router traces for trace-0a1b2c3d: routing path -> safety-classifier-v3 -> `safety_enforce` -> chat-runtime. Policy engine returned action `block_and_refuse`. Attached mini trace snippet:
```
[2026-03-10T19:12:03Z] trace-0a1b2c3d: classifier_score=0.78 threshold=0.75 action=refuse
```

sara: The customer is worried: their product depends on clinically-safe but helpful suggestions. Over-refusal is a major regression for them. They've paused rollout to all users and asked for rollback.

diego: Action plan proposal: 1) confirm exact safety classifier binary + config that served that trace; 2) repro on staging with latest and previous classifier artifacts; 3) if mismatch found, rollback the safety component for affected tenants OR add an override that reverts to previous threshold for BrightHealth until we ship a fix.

avery: Agreed. Also need to capture representative inputs from customer (we have a few in the thread) to add to the eval suite. Please mark P1 for support.

jordan: I've already flagged infra to hold the rollout. Canary increment was disabled but the initial canary was still live. I'm prepping a rollback patch to restore the previous safety config (rollback id: rb-2026-03-10-safety-001). Will coordinate with Diego on artifact verification.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] rollback initiated: rb-2026-03-10-safety-001 for safety-classifier-v3. Started 2026-03-10T20:05:41Z.

diego: I'll reproduce locally using the exact artifact sha we had before and after. Need the artifact shas — Jordan, can you share build ids?

jordan: Pre-change sha: sha256:aaa111... Post-change sha: sha256:bbb222... attaching full trace links in the internal ticket.

sara: Customer is asking for ETA on rollback. They are currently in mitigation mode and have engineers standing by. Any ETA?

jordan: Rollback started ~20:05Z. Expect 5-8 minutes to finish and routing cache TTL is 60s so should observe changes within ~2-3 minutes after rollback completes. I'll post updates.

avery: Once rollback is confirmed we should:
- run a smoke test suite (clinical QA prompts)
- gather ~20 representative queries from BrightHealth and run them against both configs
- add failing examples to eval harness and label them for future safety tuning

sara: Tell BrightHealth we'll prioritize the rollback and follow up with specific repro comparisons and a proposed remediation plan. They've asked for a postmortem after closure.

jordan: Rollback completed 2026-03-10T20:13:02Z. infra-bot shows success.

infra-bot: [deploy-bot] rollback complete: rb-2026-03-10-safety-001 status=success duration=00:07:21

jordan: I re-ran the trace for trace-0a1b2c3d repro. New classifier_score=0.60 threshold=0.72 action=allow_followup. Repro now returns a helpful assistant response sample (truncated):
```json
{"id":"r_124","model":"redwood-chat-1.1-prod","output":"You can generally take ibuprofen with lisinopril but check with your doctor...","safety_flag":"allowed","route":"normal"}
```

diego: Good. I'll run a comparative batch over the customer's sample set and post metrics (refusal rate pre/post).

avery: Also need a short KB we can share with customers explaining the canary and safety-patch process + mitigation options (pinning, tenant overrides). I'll draft and loop in legal for wording.

sara: BrightHealth responded: they see the expected behavior now. They want confirmation of the root cause before we close the ticket. They also asked for the specific rollback id to audit on their side.

jordan: Root cause hypothesis (pending full postmortem): templating bug inverted the sign/field when rendering safety_threshold for the clinical domain, causing an unintended stricter effective threshold for some deployments during the canary. Fix: template patch + add e2e check on sign and add canary telemetry to detect sudden refusal-rate deltas.

avery: I'll own the postmortem and follow-up comms. Diego, can you include the comparative metrics and the failing examples? Sara, keep the customer updated and ask if they'd like the examples redacted before we publish.

sara: Will do. Thanks everyone. :thumbsup:

--- end of thread ---
